solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: House worker perhaps, I toil furiously in dreadful panic

indicators.note: in puts the reworked toil letters inside the reworked panic letters
dreadful says the letters of panic are in a terrible state and must be rearranged
furiously says the letters of I toil are thrown about wildly into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone toils frantically at work while gripped by dreadful panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House worker perhaps' sounds like a cleaner or domestic, but the House is Parliament; 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Member of Parliament sits in the House of Commons, so an MP is one example of a House worker.

clue.text: Strike enforcer takes nothing from coal product in mine

indicators.note: in puts the shortened coal product inside the mine word

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: takes, with from, says the nothing letter is removed from the coal product

parts.note: coke is fuel made by heating coal
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A striker at a coal mine stops fuel leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'takes ... from' is split around 'nothing', which supplies the letter removed from the coal product.
explanation.definitionFit: A picket stands outside a workplace during a strike to discourage others from working.

clue.text: Pass up beer in place

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the pass word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Hand the beer up to its proper place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass up' looks like handing something over; 'up' turns COL into LOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A locale is a place or setting where something happens.

clue.text: Control ball aiming for goal in sport

parts.note: in football to trap the ball is to bring it under control
shooting is trying to score

explanation.surface: Football skills: control the ball and aim for goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface misleads: the sport is shooting at clay targets flung from a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Trapshooting is the sport of firing at clay pigeons released from a spring trap.

clue.text: What cows eat is about right for dairy product

indicators.note: is about says the cows' food goes around the right letter

parts.note: cows chew the cud

explanation.surface: What cattle feed on is just right for producing dairy goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Curd is the thick part of soured milk used to make cheese, a dairy food.

clue.text: A cricket club phone sound cut short in Stanley's place

parts.note: to ring is to phone

indicators.note: cut short says the final letter of the sound word is dropped

parts.note: a tone is a sound

explanation.surface: A cricket club's phone call ends abruptly at Stanley's home.
explanation.walkthrough: Accrington Stanley is an English football club from Accrington, a Lancashire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Accrington is the Lancashire town that gives its name to the football club Accrington Stanley.

clue.text: Writer of plays safe for audience

indicators.note: for audience says the word is to be heard by listeners rather than read

parts.note: safe in the sense of certain, a sure thing

explanation.surface: A playwright's work is a safe bet with theatregoers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent SURE and SHAW sound alike; the surface's audience is also literally a theatre crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish dramatist, author of Pygmalion and many other stage works.

clue.text: Pilot has crashed — get him here

indicators.note: crashed says the letters of pilot has are wrecked and put back in another order

explanation.surface: A pilot has crashed and needs to be taken somewhere for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue tells the story: after a crash, the pilot would be taken to the place the definition points at.
explanation.definitionFit: An injured airman would be taken to a hospital for treatment, the place where patients are cared for.

clue.text: Dignitaries or head of state beset by cats

indicators.note: beset by says the cats word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, so cats are whips

indicators.note: head of says take the first letter of state

explanation.surface: Officials or a head of state are surrounded by cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of state' looks like a title; 'head of' takes just S. Mayors and magistrates are addressed as 'Your Worship'.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship is a title of honour for mayors and magistrates, so their worships are civic dignitaries.

clue.text: Bird needs a moment, being fabulous

parts.note: a cock is a male bird, especially a rooster
in a trice means in a moment

explanation.surface: A bird requires only a moment to look wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' looks like praise, but here it means belonging to fable: the definition reads 'fabulous being'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockatrice is a mythical serpent hatched from a cock's egg, a creature of fable.

clue.text: Person in charge succeeded initially in pitch

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the word for pitch

parts.note: pitch is the black sticky substance also called tar

indicators.note: initially says take only the first letter of succeeded

explanation.surface: A leader got off to a winning start on the playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies; 'pitch' looks like a sports ground but means tar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the Russian emperor, and the word now also means an official put in charge of a policy area.

clue.text: Liberal is redrafting Parliamentary process

indicators.note: liberal in the sense of free or loose, so the letters of is redrafting are taken freely

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is redrafting a bill going through Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' poses as a politician; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The first reading is the formal introduction of a bill, the opening stage of its passage through Parliament.

clue.text: Incline to follow leaderless soldiers and join up

indicators.note: to follow says the incline word comes after the soldiers piece
leaderless says the first letter of the soldiers word is dropped

parts.note: soldiers are men in crossword shorthand
a ship that lists leans or inclines to one side

explanation.surface: Inclined to tag along behind soldiers without a commander, someone signs up.
explanation.definitionFit: To join up is to sign on for military service, the same as to enrol in the forces.

clue.text: Get little beauty outside car

indicators.note: outside says the beauty word wraps around the car word

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: Someone gets a small beauty to stand beside the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get little' looks like an instruction to obtain something small; it means become smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish is to lessen or shrink, which is to become smaller.

clue.text: One hungry celebrity covering up — not I

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: not says the letter I is left out of the covering word

parts.note: veiling is covering up

explanation.surface: A famous person, starving, covers up and denies it.
explanation.definitionFit: A starveling is a person or animal that is thin from lack of food.

clue.text: Coach in job a 1 Across means to secure delivery

indicators.note: in puts the coach word inside the job word

parts.note: a post is a job or position
a stage is a stagecoach
the answer to 1 Across, a parliamentarian, is abbreviated MP

explanation.surface: A coaching job is a way for a politician to secure a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuck-on stamp pays the fee so that a letter will be carried and delivered.

clue.text: Is act arising in long story happening from time to time

indicators.note: in puts the pieces inside the long story word

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative tale
taken as written

indicators.note: arising, in a down clue, says the act word is read upwards

parts.note: to do is to act

explanation.surface: An act rises up in a long saga that unfolds from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'arising' reverses only the act word; 'Is' stays as written beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodic means occurring at irregular intervals, now and then.

clue.text: Loudly criticises accommodation

definitions.meaning: jeers or heckles, as a crowd might a player

explanation.surface: Someone loudly complains about where they are lodged.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is to jeer at a performer, and barracks are buildings where soldiers live.

clue.text: Labrador pets destroyed building material

indicators.note: destroyed says the letters of Labrador pets are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Pet labradors have chewed up something used in building work.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasterboard is gypsum sheeting used to line interior walls, a common construction material.

clue.text: Forwards alien parcel

parts.note: in rugby the forwards are collectively called the pack
ET is the alien of the Steven Spielberg film

explanation.surface: Send on a parcel from another planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forwards' looks like a verb, sending something on; it is rugby's forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A packet is a small package or parcel.

clue.text: Ruins partly inside Bristol

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ruins lie partly inside the city of Bristol.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the scattered remains of something destroyed, which is wreckage or ruins.

clue.text: Athlete — small one making an impression

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a printer makes impressions on paper

explanation.surface: A slight athlete makes a strong impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making an impression' suggests winning admiration; it means pressing ink onto paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter is a runner who races over short distances, a kind of athlete.

clue.text: Locality around a grand house

indicators.note: around says the locality word goes about the letter a

parts.note: a place is a locality or spot

explanation.surface: The neighbourhood surrounds a large mansion.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is a large and splendid residence, typically of royalty.

clue.text: Druggie, Liverpudlian but not Scot mostly

indicators.note: but not says the following letters are removed from the Liverpudlian word

parts.note: a Scouser is someone from Liverpool

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of Scot is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before shortening

explanation.surface: A drug addict from Liverpool, but mostly not from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SCOT to SCO, and 'but not' removes SCO from SCOUSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for someone who takes illegal drugs, an addict.

clue.text: Avoid failure to score

definitions.meaning: to dodge or bob down out of the way of something
in cricket a batsman out without scoring a run is out for nought

explanation.surface: Someone sidesteps the embarrassment of not scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck is to dodge, and in cricket a zero score is called this, after the egg-shaped nought.

clue.text: Perhaps Babe's heart goes to hunter of boar

parts.note: Babe is the pig in the film of that name, so Babe's suggests pig's
ticker is slang for the heart

explanation.surface: The heart of a famous film pig is set on hunting wild boar.
explanation.walkthrough: Babe is the talking piglet of the 1995 film; 'perhaps' marks it as an example of a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigsticker hunts wild boar on horseback with a spear, or is the spear itself.

clue.text: Found players

definitions.meaning: to found metal is to shape it in a mould
the actors in a play taken together

explanation.surface: Discovered some actors.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast metal is to found it in a mould, and a cast is the company of actors in a production.

clue.text: Garage gets building concrete materials

indicators.note: building says the letters of garage gets are put together into a new structure

explanation.surface: A garage gets materials in to build with concrete.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggregates are the sand, gravel and crushed stone mixed with cement to make concrete.
